The patient's symptoms and ECG findings, including ST segment changes and new reciprocal ST depression, are consistent with myocardial infarction. The resolution of ST segment changes after catheterization also supports this diagnosis.

The patient's history of a solid and cystic hidradenoma with recurrence and positive margins, along with the clinical presentation of an enlarged, firm right ala, suggests a malignant transformation of the hidradenoma.

The patient's presentation of a tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala, with a history of a hidradenoma, could also suggest an aggressive digital papillary adenocarcinoma, given the similar immunohistochemical profile.

The skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis could suggest psoriasis, but the clinical presentation and extent of involvement are more consistent with Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.

The patient's presentation with a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal and imaging findings showing a heterogeneous lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, along with the pathological description of a tan to brown, rubbery specimen consisting of cartilage, are consistent with a diagnosis of chondrosarcoma.

The patient's symptoms of gradual-onset right facial weakness and the imaging findings showing expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal could also be consistent with a diagnosis of pleomorphic adenoma, although the pathological findings are more suggestive of chondrosarcoma.

The patient's presentation with fever, shortness of breath, and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally, along with bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography, could also be consistent with community-acquired pneumonia, although the positive nasopharyngeal swab by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction suggests a viral etiology.

The patient has a large polypoid mass in the left nasal cavity, and the pathological analysis shows CD138 and CD56 positivity, EBV positivity, and gains of fluorescence signal at multiple loci, which are characteristic of Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma

Although less likely, the gains of fluorescence signal at multiple loci, including 3q27 (BCL6), 8q24 (MYC), and 14q32 (IGH), could also be seen in Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, but the CD20 and PAX5 negativity make this diagnosis less likely

The patient's gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis, along with imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen and expansion of the fallopian canal, suggest a tumor of the facial nerve. The ocular findings, including tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility, are consistent with posterior scleritis.

The patient's sudden vision loss, along with the presence of a relative afferent pupillary defect, tortuous vessels, and serous retinal detachment, suggests a vascular occlusion. The patient's symptoms of vision loss, eye pain, and elevated intraocular pressure are consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma. The patient's presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla with progressive infiltration of the overlying skin, combined with the histopathological findings of dermal tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and the presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands, suggests cutaneous apocrine carcinoma.

The location of the tumor in the axilla, the presence of erythematous plaque, and the immunohistochemical positivity for cytokeratin 20 and GCDFP15 could also suggest extramammary Paget's disease, although the absence of epidermal involvement and the specific pattern of the tumor cells make this diagnosis less likely.

Patient's autopsy findings showed larval sections in the right eye and a coiled, incompletely sectioned filariform larva within a medium-caliber artery, which is consistent with strongyloidiasis, a parasitic infection that can cause disseminated disease in immunocompromised patients
The patient has a systolic murmur, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a large defect with left-to-right shunt, which are consistent with an atrial septal defect.

The patient's symptoms, including bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation, along with laboratory tests showing positive PCR results for Chikungunya virus in the aqueous tap and positive IgM CHIKV serologic test, suggest Chikungunya virus infection as the most likely diagnosis.

The patient's presentation with stromal immune ring formation, keratic precipitates, and mild anterior chamber reaction, following a recent infection, could also suggest post-infectious uveitis as a possible diagnosis.

The patient has a family history of prostate cancer and a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene, which is associated with Lynch syndrome.
The patient presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and underwent a dilation and curettage, which may indicate endometrial cancer, especially given the genetic predisposition to cancer.

The patient's symptoms, including pruritic papules and the presence of vacuolar degeneration of the basal cell layer, could also be consistent with Grover's disease, although the lack of specific triggers or exacerbating factors makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient presents with a large, firm, tender mass near the umbilicus, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and a large mesenteric mass abutting multiple segments of small intestine, which is suggestive of a lymphoma involving the mesenteric lymph nodes.

The patient's symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, along with the CT findings of a large mesenteric mass and diffuse lymphadenopathy, could also be consistent with mesenteric panniculitis, a rare inflammatory condition of the mesenteric fat.

Patient has hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and skin biopsy showing nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils, which are consistent with systemic mastocytosis and eosinophilic granuloma

The patient's sudden vision loss, optic disc swelling, and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, combined with the vitreous biopsy showing astrocytic neoplasm and positive immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acid protein, suggest a malignant glioma, most likely glioblastoma.

The patient's initial presentation with blurred vision, relative afferent pupillary defect, and mild swelling of the optic disc, followed by rapid progression to vision loss and optic disc swelling, could also suggest an optic nerve glioma, especially given the astrocytic neoplasm found in the vitreous biopsy.

The patient's symptoms of a swollen right upper eyelid with pus discharge, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, suggest a diagnosis of frontal sinus mucocele.

The patient's long history of symptoms, lack of trauma, and imaging findings of sinus opacification and mild inflammatory infiltrate on histopathology suggest a diagnosis of chronic frontal sinusitis.

The patient's biopsy showed a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, which is consistent with B-cell lymphoma. The presence of a large, firm ulcer on the penis and systemic symptoms such as fatigue and weight loss also support this diagnosis.

top2_diagnoses.diagnosis: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
top2_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation with a large, painful ulcer on the penis, which is an unusual site for lymphoma, and the presence of atypical lymphocytes with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, suggests a diagnosis of primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The leg type is a subtype that often presents with leg or skin involvement.

The patient's lesion is characterized by discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque, which is consistent with angiosarcoma. The KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R mutation identified through paired whole-exome sequencing also supports this diagnosis.

The patient's lesion is a well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, which could also be consistent with pyogenic granuloma. However, the presence of the KDR (VEGFR2) mutation and the specific histopathological features make angiosarcoma a more likely diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms, including subacute progressive symmetric lower extremity weakness, urinary retention, and violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis), along with the laboratory findings of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid, are consistent with leukemia.

The patient's presentation of a rapidly growing, centrally ulcerated purpuric patch with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with biopsy findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells, suggests angiosarcoma.

The patient's symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance, combined with left atrial enlargement on echocardiogram, could suggest hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, although the echocardiogram does not explicitly show left ventricular hypertrophy.
The patient has a history of thyroid surgery and now presents with a lytic lesion in the manubrium, which contains follicular thyroid cells, suggesting metastasis from the previous thyroid cancer.
The presence of thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae in the manubrial lesion, as seen on pathological examination, supports the diagnosis of thyroid metastasis to bone.

The patient presents with fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, which are common symptoms of COVID-19. The nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction also supports this diagnosis.
The patient has symptoms of pneumonia, including fever, shortness of breath, and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally, and the chest radiography suggests bilateral multifocal pneumonia.

Given the clinical presentation and the histopathological findings, another possible diagnosis could be a form of histiocytosis, although Langerhans cell histiocytosis is more specific and likely given the CD1A staining.
